leakage_inflation.explanation: Contaminated ML saw 76/107 holdout drugs during training, inflating ML AAFE from 3.057 to 2.340 (23.5%). Meta-learner inherited this, inflating from 2.808 to 2.283 (18.8%). %2-fold inflated from 45.8% to 53.3% (+7.5pp).

remediation_steps: 2026-04-04: Identified 76 holdout drugs in ML training data via 3-key audit (SMILES, InChIKey14, name)
2026-04-04: Retrained xgboost_cmax, xgboost_fup_v2, xgboost_peff, xgboost_clint excluding all 107 holdout drugs
2026-04-04: Re-optimized meta-learner weights via LOOCV on clean predictions
2026-04-08: Regenerated 3track_holdout_predictions.json with clean pipeline (107 drugs × 3 tracks)
2026-04-08: Regenerated Figure 2 scatter plot with clean AAFE=2.808 annotation

engine.note: Engine uses ADME models (fup, peff, clint) which were retrained. Minimal change because engine is mechanistic — ADME predictions are just one input among many.

ml.note: ML track most affected. 76 holdout drugs leaked into training, allowing model to memorize their Cmax values directly.

clf.note: CL/F analytical model is parameter-free (no training), unaffected by contamination.

meta.note: Meta-learner inherited ML contamination. Clean weights also changed: base w_engine 0.45→0.60, non-base w_ml 1.00→0.50 (CL/F now contributes 0.15).
